youtube_title: My uncle has never paid full price for anything. Then he met my hot cocoa stand ☕
description:
Uncle Bernard has never paid full price in his life, and Penny's hot cocoa costs five dollars. Coupons, sad stories and a very slow walk away. Penny was ready for all of it.

#cartoon #animation #funny #family #shorts
tiktok_caption: my uncle has never paid full price for anything ☕ #cartoon #animation #funny #family

lines.text: Hot cocoa, five dollars? Sweetheart. I have never paid full price for anything.
Hi, Uncle Bernard. It is five dollars.
Hello. I am the cocoa pot. This man once haggled with a parking meter.
The cocoa is five dollars. The marshmallows are free.
Free is my favorite price. Give me only the marshmallows.
He wants a cup of marshmallows. That is not a drink. That is a pillow.
Okay. Opening offer. One dollar and a very nice compliment.
No.
You did not even hear the compliment.
Is it about my hat?
It was about your hat. That is a beautiful hat.
Five dollars.
She is nine years old and made of stone.
Fine. I have coupons. I always have coupons.
He pulled a binder out of his vest. The binder has a binder inside it.
This coupon is for one free cocoa.
That coupon is for a gas station. In Ohio. From two thousand eleven.
Cocoa is cocoa. Ohio is very close if you believe.
Five dollars.
Okay. A sad story. I walked here. In the cold. Uphill.
He drove. His car is right there. It is still running.
Uphill in my heart, Cocoa Pot.
Last move. The walk away. Watch me walk away.
He is looking over his shoulder. He tripped on the curb. Nobody called him.
I am back. I have decided to give you another chance.
Hi, Penny. One hot cocoa, please. Here is five dollars.
Thank you, Aunt Celeste. Here are extra marshmallows. And a cookie.
A cookie? She paid full price and got a cookie?
Bernard, you are haggling with a child again.
She started it. She has a sign. Signs are basically haggling.
Okay, Uncle Bernard. Final offer. Two dollars.
Two dollars! I did it! I beat the system! Write it down, Cocoa Pot!
Two dollars. Thank you for your business.
Penny, sweetie, why is the price on the back of the sign different?
Oh. That is the real price.
Flip the sign. The back says, cocoa, one dollar.
One dollar. The real price was one dollar.
The front says five because I knew you were coming.
She did not raise the price for the town. She raised it for one uncle.
I paid double. I have never paid double in my life.
You paid five times more than a coupon from Ohio.
Uncle Bernard, you are my best customer. You always come back.
Where did you even learn this?
From you. At the yard sale. You sold Grandma her own lamp.
He did. She paid twenty dollars for her own lamp.
It is a nice lamp. She still has it. She still does not know.
Penny. For the first time in my life, I want to pay full price.
Great. Full price for you is now seven dollars.
Five fifty and a compliment.
Seven.
